DOCS-001.title: User document uploads
DOCS-001.description: Add the ability for users to upload documents, view their list of uploaded documents, and delete a document they own.

artifacts.summary: Role-agnostic user document upload/list/delete on local disk (Docker volume), behind JwtAuthGuard; new Document Prisma model, documents Nest module, DocumentDto in packages/types, multipart-safe api-client methods, UI in apps/web /account.

details.rawPlan:
TASK: DOCS-001
TITLE: User document uploads (upload, list, delete own documents)

REQUIREMENTS:
- Add a Document model to apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma: id, userId (FK -> User, onDelete: Cascade), originalName, storedName (server-generated), mimeType, sizeBytes, createdAt. Index on userId.
- Scope: any authenticated User, ownership by userId not role. Assumption: customer-facing UI in apps/web /account area only for this task.
- Storage decision (assumption): local disk on the API container behind a named Docker volume, not S3/GCS — repo has no existing object-storage integration; every current 'image' field is a pasted URL string.
- New NestJS documents module (apps/api/src/documents/) behind JwtAuthGuard: POST /api/documents (multipart upload via FileInterceptor), GET /api/documents (list mine), GET /api/documents/:id (authenticated download, ownership-checked, never served via static assets), DELETE /api/documents/:id (ownership-checked).
- packages/types: DocumentDto + schema. packages/api-client: listMyDocuments/uploadDocument/deleteDocument, including a multipart-safe request path (client.ts request() currently force-sets application/json).
- apps/web: list/upload/delete UI in the existing /account page.
- Infra: persistent named volume for uploads in docker-compose.prod.yml; UPLOADS_DIR env var.

ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Upload returns a DocumentDto and appears in the user's list.
- Download works for the owner; another user's document id -> 404.
- Delete works for the owner (204), removes DB row + file; other user's id / nonexistent id -> 404.
- All 4 endpoints require auth (401 if not).
- Oversized upload rejected, no orphan row/file. Disallowed MIME type rejected.
- apps/web account page supports list/upload/delete with the existing auth-redirect behavior.
- pnpm typecheck and pnpm build pass after rebuilding packages/types and packages/api-client.

DEPENDENCIES:
- None on other tasks. Internal order: Prisma schema/migration -> packages/types (rebuild) -> packages/api-client (rebuild) -> apps/api documents module -> apps/web UI.
- Infra: docker-compose.prod.yml volume must land before/with first prod deploy or uploaded files are lost on next deploy (containers recreated fresh each deploy).

EDGE_CASES:
- Path traversal via originalName — never use it to build the disk path, only the server-generated storedName.
- MIME-type spoofing — extension/Content-Type filtering is a usability guard only, not a security guarantee; true content scanning out of scope, must be documented as a known limitation.
- Zero-byte upload rejected.
- File-write/DB-insert partial failure must not orphan a file or a row; download/delete should tolerate a missing file gracefully.
- Concurrent double-click delete -> second request 404s cleanly, not 500.
- No existing per-user quota pattern to copy — propose a reasonable default cap, enforced server-side.
- Redeploy without the volume wired up silently wipes files — must be caught in review.
- User account deletion cascades the DB rows (Cascade FK) but does NOT delete the files on disk automatically — needs explicit handling or an accepted, stated gap.
- Large/slow uploads — verify global ValidationPipe/body-size limits and any reverse-proxy body-size limit don't reject the multipart body before multer's own limits apply; needs checking against production Nginx config.
- Non-ASCII (Cyrillic) filenames must round-trip correctly for display.

FILES_LIKELY_AFFECTED:
- apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma
- apps/api/src/documents/ (new module, modeled on apps/api/src/support/)
- apps/api/src/main.ts (body-size limit interaction)
- apps/api/package.json / .env.example (@types/multer, UPLOADS_DIR)
- packages/types/src/schemas.ts, index.ts
- packages/api-client/src/client.ts
- apps/web/src/app/account/page.tsx (or a new nested route)
- docker-compose.prod.yml

TASK-8214d04b.title: Post-deploy health check gate
TASK-8214d04b.description: Add a GET /api/health endpoint to the API (no auth, cheap DB ping) if one doesn't already exist, and add a health-check step to .github/workflows/deploy.yml right after 'docker compose up -d' that curls https://api.gulyaly.pro/api/health with retries (e.g. up to ~30s of retrying) and fails the deploy job if it never returns 200 -- so a container that dies right after startup is caught by CI instead of silently going live broken.

artifacts.summary: Add a plain GET /api/health endpoint (new HealthModule, no auth, Prisma $queryRaw SELECT 1 to prove DB connectivity) and a curl-with-retry gate in deploy.yml's deploy step, run inside the existing SSH block right after docker compose up -d against the container's local port (127.0.0.1:4000), not the public domain -- avoids DNS/TLS/nginx as confounding variables in the CI gate itself. Job fails (ssh session's own non-zero exit, set -e) if health never returns 200 within the retry window.

No UI surface for this task -- reviewed Planner's spec: a JSON health endpoint consumed only by the CI deploy job's curl step, no page/component/user-facing flow anywhere in apps/web, apps/admin, or apps/seller. Nothing to design; Developer can implement directly from Planner's spec.

Implemented GET /api/health (new HealthModule/Controller, no auth, Prisma SELECT 1 -> 200 ok / 503 ServiceUnavailableException on DB failure) and a curl-with-retry gate in deploy.yml's SSH deploy block right after docker compose up -d (127.0.0.1:4000, up to 15x/2s = ~30s, exits non-zero before migrate deploy runs if never healthy). 2/2 new jest tests pass, full apps/api suite 15/15 green, pnpm typecheck and pnpm build clean, live-verified against a local dev boot (curl -> 200 {status:ok}). Committed on feature/health-check-gate (bd2104d), not main.

Independently re-ran: full apps/api jest suite (15/15, incl. the 2 new health tests), pnpm typecheck + pnpm build clean, diff scope check clean (only health/ + app.module.ts + deploy.yml touched, no creep). Parsed deploy.yml with js-yaml to confirm it's still valid YAML and the single-quoted remote ssh script wasn't broken by the new bash block (no stray single quotes), then bash -n'd the extracted script for syntax. Live-verified the exact retry-loop logic on the actual production VPS (not just locally) against two real conditions: (1) closed port -> curl fails in ~15ms real time on the Linux box (my initial Windows/git-bash test showed a misleading ~2s-per-attempt artifact, ruled out as environment-specific, not a real issue); (2) against the currently-deployed (pre-this-feature) api container's real /api/health 404 -- loop correctly retried 15x and exited 1 after ~30s wall-clock, matching the code's own "after 30s" log message. No blocking findings.

Reviewed health.controller.ts, health.module.ts, app.module.ts diff, and the deploy.yml change. No auth on GET /api/health is correct/intentional (health endpoints must be reachable by CI/monitoring without credentials) and leaks nothing sensitive -- response is a static {status:ok} or a generic 503 message, never the raw DB error. $queryRaw is a static parameterless literal (SELECT 1), zero injection surface -- no user input anywhere in this endpoint. Still covered by the existing global ThrottlerGuard, so it's not an unthrottled DoS vector. deploy.yml change adds no new secrets and doesn't touch existing secret handling; the curl target is a hardcoded 127.0.0.1 literal, no SSRF. No new npm dependency. Not applicable: IDOR, money/balance races, DTO validation (no request body/params exist). One non-blocking note: health.controller.ts's catch block discards the real Prisma error before throwing ServiceUnavailableException -- fine for the public response, but means ops has zero server-log signal for *why* health failed beyond docker/prisma logs elsewhere; recommend a Logger.warn(err) before the throw, same pattern as the existing non-blocking note on DOCS-001's users.service.ts. Not blocking.

pnpm build clean. No Prisma migration needed (no schema change). Full docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile completed end-to-end this time (7m19s, not just inspected/caveated like DOCS-001's) -> ran the actual built image against local dev Postgres/Redis, confirmed HealthController {/api/health} mapped and curl returned 200 {status:ok} from the real production artifact, not just nest start --watch dev mode. Cleaned up test container/image after.

Cold-start race test: started the real built image with zero warm-up delay and began the exact deploy.yml retry loop immediately. Container wasn't listening yet on tries 1-2 (still booting), succeeded on try 3 (~4-6s in) -- concretely proves the retry window bridges a real startup gap, not just a theoretical one. Confirms the feature does what it's for. Cleaned up container + image after.

Merged feature/health-check-gate into main (fast-forward, bd2104d) and pushed. deploy.yml run 32521164332: build-and-test (2m12s), build-images (5m4s), deploy (1m41s) -- all green, including the new health-check retry step inside the deploy job (would have failed the job if unhealthy). Live-verified post-deploy on the VPS: curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/api/health -> 200 {status:ok}; docker compose ps shows api/web/admin freshly recreated (~1min uptime) and healthy.

TASK-7e0a6540.title: Referral program with auto-generated changeable username
TASK-7e0a6540.description: Port and adapt the well-designed referral system already built on the (unmerged, stale) feature/sku-username-referrals branch (based at commit 0d4cff2, missing this session's 16 commits worth of main -- Document model, health-check, SSL automation, agent-orchestrator, monitoring page) onto current main. That branch's design (see apps/api/src/referrals/referrals.service.ts and the schema.prisma diff on that branch): User.referralCode (unique, auto-generated 8-char alphanumeric at registration, retry-loop for uniqueness), User.referredByCode/referredById (denormalized audit trail), User.referralBalanceTmt (accrued reward), a Referral model tracking PENDING->REWARDED->VOID lifecycle keyed to a qualifying order, a ReferralSettings singleton (enabled toggle + configurable customer/seller reward amounts), automatic capped discount applied at order-creation via a race-safe conditional updateMany (not read-then-write), and an admin ledger/leaderboard page. Sellers already use their existing Seller.handle (already on main) as their own referral code -- do not duplicate that. NEW requirement not in the old branch: the user must be able to CHANGE their auto-generated referralCode/username later (uniqueness re-checked on change, reject duplicates). Do NOT port the old branch's apps/seller extraction or its seller-login-by-handle auth.service.ts changes -- out of scope, unrelated, and would conflict with this session's work already on main. Must coexist cleanly with the current Document model and everything else added to main since 0d4cff2. This is a prerequisite for the separate 'full profile editing' task, which will surface/let the user change this username in the apps/web account page.

artifacts.summary: Read current main's User/Seller/Order models, auth.service.ts (register/login/changePassword/getMe/updateMe already exist!), users.service.ts SAFE_SELECT, and the full referrals.service.ts + admin referrals.tsx from the stale feature/sku-username-referrals branch. Plan: rename the branch's 'referralCode' concept to 'username' (schema field User.username, unique, auto-generated 8-char lowercase alphanumeric at registration with retry-loop, changeable via new PATCH endpoint). Critical cross-table uniqueness edge case identified and must be handled: Seller.handle (already on main, sellers' own referral code) and User.username are separate unique constraints on separate tables -- generation AND the new change-username endpoint must check BOTH tables to prevent a customer picking a username that collides with an existing seller handle (silent shadowing: resolveReferrerByUsername checks seller.handle first, so a colliding user username would never resolve to that user). New Referral model (PENDING/REWARDED/VOID lifecycle), ReferralSettings singleton, Order.referralDiscountTmt, race-safe discount application (conditional updateMany, not read-then-write) and idempotent reward-on-qualifying-order -- port directly from the branch's proven design. Admin referrals.tsx ports near-verbatim (settings/leaderboard/ledger UI already matches existing admin conventions). Do NOT port the branch's apps/seller extraction or seller-login-by-handle changes -- unrelated, out of scope, would conflict with this session's main.

Only UI surface for this task is the admin Referrals page (customer-facing username display/edit belongs to the dependent TASK-474505ac). Reference implementation from the branch (admin/src/pages/referrals.tsx) already follows this app's exact conventions -- Card/Button/Input primitives, table patterns identical to other admin list pages, settings toggle matching existing form patterns elsewhere. Porting near-verbatim, only renaming the 'code' field references to 'username' to match the renamed schema field. Three sections: Settings (enabled toggle + reward amounts form), Leaderboard (7/30-day range toggle, ranked by referral count), Ledger (last 200 referrals, referrer/referee/username/status/reward/date). Nav entry + route registration follow the identical pattern as every other admin page (App.tsx + layout.tsx navItems).

Ported and adapted the referral system: migration (username nullable->backfilled with own cuid id for existing rows->NOT NULL+unique, avoiding any collision risk; new Referral/ReferralSettings tables), referrals module (service/controller/DTOs), auth.service.ts register() now generates a username via ReferralsService and records the referral fire-and-forget, login/getMe/updateMe expose username. Wired into sellers.service.ts (seller's User.username = their handle, cross-checked against existing usernames in assertPhoneAndHandleFree) and users.service.ts (staff creation generates a username too) since username is now a required unique column on every User row. Orders integration: create() applies a race-safe referral-balance discount against amountTmt (recipient still gets full value, customer pays less), processTopup() rewards the referrer when the referee's order completes. 12 new unit tests (cross-table username collision, race-condition fallback to 409, discount capping, self-referral guard, disabled-program no-op) + full existing suite all green (39/39). Full monorepo typecheck clean. Live E2E verified via curl end-to-end: register with referral code -> stats show pending:1 -> complete referee's order -> reward credited (referralBalanceTmt +10) -> new order for referrer auto-discounts (verified exact math: 50 TMT - 10 balance = 40 TMT charged) -> balance drained to 0 -> username change tested (409 on collision with existing user, 200 on free name) -> admin ledger/leaderboard verified showing correct denormalized old username even after the referrer changed their username. Admin Referrals page ported, live-verified in browser rendering real data (settings values, leaderboard, ledger).

Independently verified: (1) checked schema.prisma directly -- referralDiscountTmt exists ONLY on Order, not GalleryOrder (confirmed the migrate-dev diff noise mentioning GalleryOrder was comparing against the OLD branch-drifted DB state pre-reset, not the actual applied migration -- migrate status confirms clean/up-to-date now). (2) Traced partner-API order path (apiKeyId-attributed, no userId): both the discount-application and reward-crediting code paths are guarded by /, so partner orders correctly skip referral logic entirely with no crash risk. (3) Confirmed RolesGuard uses getAllAndOverride, so the method-level @Roles('ADMIN') on the settings PATCH correctly overrides the controller-level @Roles('ADMIN','MANAGER') -- managers can view settings but only full admins can change reward amounts, matching the existing pattern used elsewhere in this codebase. (4) Re-ran full test suite independently (39/39) and full monorepo typecheck (clean). No blocking findings.

Reviewed the full diff. No auth bypass: username-change endpoint requires JwtAuthGuard, operates only on the caller's own userId (no IDOR -- there is no id parameter accepted from the client for this mutation). Race conditions: applyReferralDiscount uses a conditional updateMany (gte check + decrement in one atomic statement), not read-then-write -- matches the pattern this codebase already required for money-touching code (Seller.balanceTmt precedent). changeUsername has a pre-check plus a P2002 catch as the real safety net against a concurrent-change race -- correct defense in depth. Injection: no raw SQL anywhere in the new code, all Prisma query builder. Input validation: class-validator on both new DTOs, username format enforced server-side via a regex (not just client-side), independent of whatever the admin UI or apps/web later send. Business logic abuse checks: self-referral blocked (referrerUserId === refereeUserId), a bad/garbage referral code at registration is swallowed in a try-catch so it can never DoS or fail signups, reward crediting is idempotent (checks status still PENDING before paying out, so re-processing an order or a retried queue job cannot double-pay). Data exposure: username is intentionally public/shareable (it's a referral code), no secret fields (passwordHash, tokenHash) touched by any new select clause. No blocking findings.

pnpm build clean across all 7 packages (full monorepo), typecheck clean. Migration applied and verified against a real (reset-to-clean) local Postgres, no drift. Live E2E already covered in the developer/QA stages above.

Cold-start staging validation: killed the api dev process, restarted from scratch, confirmed ReferralsController + AdminReferralsController map cleanly on boot with no DI errors. Full referral lifecycle re-verified against the freshly-started process (register with code -> pending -> order completes -> reward credited -> discount applied on a new order -> username change -> admin ledger/leaderboard render real data in the browser). Sits at the production_deployment gate now alongside its dependent TASK-474505ac; per user instruction both wait for local review before deploy.

TASK-474505ac.title: Full customer profile editing on account page
TASK-474505ac.description: The apps/web /account page currently only shows order history and the documents section (DOCS-001) -- there is no way for a customer to edit their own info. Add a proper profile editor: full name, phone number, password change (requires current password), and a profile picture (avatar upload -- follow the existing Document upload pattern in apps/api/src/documents/ for local-disk storage conventions, but this is a distinct concern: one avatar per user, replaces on re-upload rather than accumulating, no per-user quota needed). Reviewed the diff. Avatar public GET is a deliberate design choice (documented in code comments), not an oversight -- avatars carry no secret data, and the storedName is a random UUID never derived from user input, validated by a strict regex before any filesystem access, so no path traversal and no enumeration beyond guessing UUIDs. Upload/delete require JwtAuthGuard and act only on req.user.userId -- no id parameter accepted from the client, so no IDOR is possible on either endpoint. No new auth bypass, no secret fields exposed in any new select clause. One accepted, explicitly-documented limitation carried over from the Document module's existing precedent: file-type filtering is by declared Content-Type header only, not actual content sniffing -- consistent with, not a regression from, the existing security posture.
